## 2. Missing trials




::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
rt2 <- c(523, NA, 487, 150, 601, 455, 2310, NA, 512, 498)

sum(is.na(rt2)); which(is.na(rt2))
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
[1] 2
```


:::

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
[1] 2 8
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
mean(rt2, na.rm = TRUE)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
[1] 692
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}

sum(implausible, na.rm = TRUE)
```

## 3. Spot the bugs




::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
scores <- c(12, 15, 9, 20, 17)
group <- c("a", "b", "a", "b", "a")
mean(scores[group == "a"])   # = instead of ==, and a missing )
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
[1] 12.66667
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
mean(scores[group == "b"])   # maen
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
[1] 17.5
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
mean(scores)                 # Mean: R is case-sensitive
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
[1] 14.6
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
summary(scores)              # Scores
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
   Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 
    9.0    12.0    15.0    14.6    17.0    20.0 
```


:::
:::




The silent one is `=` instead of `==`. Inside `[ ]`, `group = "a"` does not compare anything: R reads it as `scores["a"]`, the element named `"a"`. There is none, so you get `NA` and no error.

## 4. A Likert item




::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
answers <- c("often", "never", "sometimes", "always", "often", "rarely",
             "sometimes", "often", "never", "always", "sometimes", "often")
table(answers)     # alphabetical: "always" comes first
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
answers
   always     never     often    rarely sometimes 
        2         2         4         1         3 
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
lev <- c("never", "rarely", "sometimes", "often", "always")
answers_f <- factor(answers, levels = lev, ordered = TRUE)
table(answers_f)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
answers_f
    never    rarely sometimes     often    always 
        2         1         3         4         2 
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
score <- as.numeric(answers_f)
mean(score)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
[1] 3.25
```


:::
:::

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
factor(c(answers, "Often"), levels = lev, ordered = TRUE)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
 [1] often     never     sometimes always    often     rarely    sometimes
 [8] often     never     always    sometimes often     <NA>     
Levels: never < rarely < sometimes < often < always
```


:::
:::




`"Often"` is not one of the levels (case-sensitive), so it becomes `NA`, silently. Check with `sum(is.na(...))` after building a factor.

## 5. A data frame by hand




::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
participants <- data.frame(
  id    = c("P01", "P02", "P03", "P04", "P05", "P06"),
  group = factor(c("patient", "control", "patient", "control", "patient", "control")),
  age   = c(72, 65, 68, 70, 61, 74),
  score = c(21, 29, 23, 28, 25, 27)
)
str(participants)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
'data.frame':	6 obs. of  4 variables:

 $ age  : num  72 65 68 70 61 74
 $ score: num  21 29 23 28 25 27
```

## 6. Your first functions




::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
se <- function(x) {
  sd(x, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(sum(!is.na(x)))   # length() would count the NA
}
se(rt_clean)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
[1] 16.22241
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
se(rt2)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
[1] 235.9161
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
n_outliers <- function(x, low = 200, high = 1500) {
  sum(x < low | x > high, na.rm = TRUE)
}
n_outliers(rt2)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
[1] 2
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
n_outliers(rt2, high = 600)   # 601 now counts too
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
[1] 3
```


:::

# Part 2: Quarto

## 9. Your first report

A table of contents appears in a left sidebar. All HTML options: <https://quarto.org/docs/reference/formats/html.html>.

```markdown
### My project

I study **sleep** in *university students* using:

- questionnaires
- a sleep diary
- reaction times

More on the [Quarto website](https://quarto.org).
```

## 10. Bring in your analysis

````markdown
```{{r}}
#| echo: false
sleepstudy <- read.csv(here::here("data", "sleepstudy.csv"))
```

```{{r}}
base <- sleepstudy[sleepstudy$Days == 2, ]
day9 <- sleepstudy[sleepstudy$Days == 9, ]
change <- day9$Reaction - base$Reaction
```

```{{r}}
#| label: fig-change
#| fig-cap: "Change in reaction time from baseline (day 2) to day 9, one value per subject."
hist(change, xlab = "Change in reaction time (ms)", main = NULL)
```
````




::: {.cell}
::: {.cell-output-display}
![Change in reaction time from baseline (day 2) to day 9, one value per subject.](solutions_files/figure-html/fig-change-1.png){#fig-change width=672}
:::
:::




`@fig-change` becomes a numbered, clickable "Figure 1". With `echo: false` the chunk still runs, but its code is hidden. This chunk prints nothing, so it disappears from the report.

## 11. Numbers in the text

```markdown
After 7 nights with 3 hours in bed, reaction time increased by `{{r}} round(mean(change))` ms
on average; `{{r}} sum(change > 0)` of `{{r}} length(change)` subjects slowed down (@fig-change).
```

> After 7 nights with 3 hours in bed, reaction time increased by 85 ms on average; 16 of 18 subjects slowed down (@fig-change).

```markdown
On average, patients slept `{{r}} round(mean(d21), 2)` hours more with drug 2 than with drug 1,
and `{{r}} sum(d21 > 0)` out of 10 slept more with drug 2.
```

> On average, patients slept 1.58 hours more with drug 2 than with drug 1, and 9 out of 10 slept more with drug 2.
